title: Prior Deferment Agreements and the Home Purchase Financing Good-Faith Payment
content:
**Loss mitigation committee note — repeat hardship on Home Purchase Financing loans**

Where two or more deferment agreements were signed on the loan in the 36 whole months before the payment date, the good-faith repeat multiplier is 1.5; where exactly one was signed in those 36 months, the good-faith repeat multiplier is 1.2. Where none was signed in those 36 months, no repeat multiplier applies.

The multiplier applies to the good-faith payment amount before it is rounded; the good-faith payment is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end. The agreements counted are the deferment agreements recorded on the loan's notices, by their dates.

| Deferment agreements signed in the 36 whole months before the payment date | Good-faith repeat multiplier |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 1.5 |
| exactly 1 | 1.2 |
| none | none applies |

*Hypothetical example.* An unrounded good-faith amount of 260.685 with one agreement in the 36 months becomes 260.685 times 1.2, that is 312.822, which rounds to 312.82. With two agreements it becomes 391.0275, which rounds to 391.03.
